label: XV
reasoning: The rewrite was an accepted instruction, and the verification step is satisfied: plan_checks.py exits 0 and names each rewritten row, and the regenerated board page shows the new titles -- this is a command and a plain read confirming the observable outcome named at acceptance (eleven titles reading as plain sentences), not merely that work began. Under "A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery," the Director shows the result and closes the checkpoint in the same step once the verifier confirms the outcome; it never leaves the row open waiting for the person to look at and bless what was already shown, unless the row's own definition of done actually names his eye as the check -- and here it does not, since wording of internal jargon into plain language is a mechanical rewrite checked by plan_checks.py and a regenerated page, not a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct. It is also not an irreversible action under rule 12/27 -- rewriting queue titles in PLAN.md is a reversible edit, not a case requiring his word before it runs. That the person hasn't seen it yet, and that it is the middle of the night, is not itself a reason to hold: if he later disagrees with a shown result, that disagreement is a new fact handled as its own task carrying his correction, and the closed row stays closed.
